vb1_reasoning: The previous reviewer's finding was that the writeOnly read-direction rule was unobservable redundancy - an equivalent mutant, because the credential-leak property was already enforced by other layers ($defs/CredentialSummary + additionalProperties:false on the response side, firstSensitiveKey red list on the durable-event side). The added pair now isolates the rule itself, and the isolation is real rather than claimed: (1) the value under test is the single writeOnly annotation the pinned contract actually declares (NativeCredentialImportRequest.credential_value, confirmed by walking the fixture - one occurrence, no others), (2) it is structurally schema-legal, since disabling the rule makes ValidateDef return nil (the failure detail literally reads <nil>), which proves no JSON-Schema keyword and no other guard can reject that value in read direction - i.e. the direction rule is the ONLY thing that can fail WRITE-ONLY-DEF-READ-DIRECTION-REJECTED, (3) the same value is still accepted in write direction in that very same mutated run, so the pair expresses the direction asymmetry rather than a blanket rejection, (4) the mutation now makes the suite exit 1 with a named failing id, so the rule is no longer self-certifying redundancy. I accept closure. One honest limit worth recording, and it is not a reversal of VB-1: the assertion calls SchemaDoc.ValidateDef/ValidateDefInput directly on a def that the contract reserves for the native-transient write path, so it observes the production direction rule at the API surface rather than through an end-to-end read path that would genuinely carry a NativeCredentialImportRequest. That end-to-end credential-never-returns-back property is what the other, already-asserted layers cover. Non-vacuity on the write side holds by construction: ValidateDefInput hard-codes allowWriteOnly=true, so any mutation that collapses the two directions fails READ-DIRECTION-REJECTED while any mutation that removes the write allowance fails ALLOWED-IN-DIRECTION - each id has its own distinct minimal mutation.
